milestones.title: D1 — Institutional & Data Source Mapping
milestones.objective: Build the first systematic institutional evidence base for Évora and expand the civic data-source catalogue without searching for software ideas.

milestones.title: D2 — Public Signal Discovery
milestones.objective: Test whether the nine institutionally identified PRB-* problems from D1 are visible in current public/lived signals, and enrich the D1 problem map with journey/context/contradiction evidence without measuring prevalence or selecting solutions.

milestones.title: D3 — Problem Map v1 & Decision Baseline
milestones.objective: Transform the D1/D2 evidence corpus into a proportionate, auditable decision baseline for every canonical active PRB-*, without prematurely selecting solutions or a civic product. See docs/milestones/D3-problem-map-decision-baseline.md and docs/discovery/d3-execution-protocol.md.

milestones.title: D4 — Existing Solutions, Comparative Evidence & Residual Gap Analysis
milestones.objective: Test the two D3-routed residual opportunity areas (PRB-0005 parking/data legibility, PRB-0009 waste service/data) against current local solutions and bounded comparative evidence, then decide whether a material residual gap remains before D5 stakeholder challenge/validation. D4 does not select a product, vendor, architecture or project.

milestones.title: D5 — Stakeholder Challenge & Validation
milestones.objective: Challenge the current Problem framings with the minimum credible direct operator, institutional, affected-journey and observational evidence needed to resolve decision-critical unknowns, refine or falsify those framings, and update validation_status only through a human-authored decision supported by proportionate direct challenge. D5 does not attempt to maximize validated PRBs.

milestones.title: M006 — D6 Evaluation Readiness
milestones.objective: Determine, through a bounded canonical screen and human gate, whether any current PRB has a sufficiently defined, measurable, locally grounded evaluation route; explicitly retain all other PRBs as conditional, hold, watch, or outside D6.

milestones.title: M007 — PRB-0009 Decision-Critical Research Carry
milestones.objective: Determine whether already-produced aggregate, comparable and legitimately accessible operational metrics can resolve the D6 uncertainty around the waste-service restructuring sufficiently for a later human readiness decision. M007 is a bounded research follow-up to D6, not a general D7 programme phase.

milestones.title: AR-01 — Research Trust Baseline
milestones.objective: Establish the post-audit research trust baseline by resolving or explicitly verifying the approved targeted canonical findings, hardening the approved mechanical validation gaps, and making the repository publication boundary unambiguous.

milestones.title: M009 — AR-02 Explorer Functional Foundation
milestones.objective: Establish a reliable functional Explorer baseline before knowledge-first product/design evolution by resolving the eight approved MUST ADDRESS functional findings (ODM-013, ODM-014, ODM-015, ODM-016, ODM-017, ODM-019, ODM-020, ODM-021) without redesigning the product or changing canonical research semantics. Graph-validation contract: the pre-existing owner-acknowledged C008/C009/C010 checkpoint packet-reference findings are historical debt, are reported separately, must not be repaired, suppressed, mutated, or re-acknowledged, and alone never constitute an AR-02 failure; any new graph finding is blocking.

milestones.title: AR-03 Knowledge-First Product Design: Foundation Consolidation
milestones.objective: Consolidate the Explorer's legacy production foundation (index.css's own hex-literal variables, ad hoc selectors, and Inter-based interface typography) onto the semantic DS-04B foundation tokens already imported into production via tokens.css (DS-05A), under the owner-frozen Public Sans interface family, without adopting foundations.css/layout.css wholesale, without any structural/component/navigation/layout redesign, and without treating DS-04B's remaining numeric/token candidates as frozen beyond what this milestone's own implementation and verification earn. Interface font is owner-frozen as Public Sans; reading font remains Source Serif 4; technical font remains IBM Plex Mono. Remaining DS-04B numeric/token values used by this migration become owner-frozen foundation values for the M010 migration scope only after successful WU036 implementation, WU037 independent production-rendered verification, and explicit owner M010 closure -- they are not previously-unused values and not universally 'newly-adopted production facts' beyond this migration's bounded scope. Short-record inline rail remains deferred. No AR-04 Problem Experience, AR-05 Discovery & Provenance, or D7 scope is included.

milestones.title: AR-04 Knowledge-First Problem Experience
milestones.objective: Transform the existing public Problem experience from a technically complete canonical projection into a coherent knowledge-first reading experience in which a reader can understand what the problem is, its current lifecycle/investigation state, what the canonical evidence establishes, the important boundaries and limits of that evidence, what remains uncertain or open, the current response/action context where canonical data supports it, and how to inspect the already-linked supporting material when needed, without changing canonical research meaning or inventing conclusions. AR-04 builds on the existing Problem View rather than creating a second Problem product model. It preserves canonical research semantics, existing canonical PRB identity, current routing/deep-link guarantees unless an exact AR-04 problem requires a bounded change, generic/shared component boundaries already established by the design system, M010 owner-frozen DS-04B foundation values, and accessibility and responsive contracts. M010-frozen DS-04B values must not be changed incidentally; any discovered need to change a frozen value is an owner decision, not delegated to AR-04 implementation. Out of scope: canonical research edits or reinterpretation, new external research, new fields/schema semantics merely to improve presentation, Records redesign, Overview redesign, Source/Evidence detail redesign except a strictly required bounded navigation handoff, global search/discovery redesign, cross-record provenance/discovery architecture (reserved for AR-05), Graph work, new product/solution selection, broad navigation redesign, foundation/token redesign, changing M010 owner-frozen DS-04B values, general CSS cleanup/refactoring, historical C008/C009/C010 repair, D7, AR-05, and unrelated deferred design debt (pre-existing body/some-navigation system-ui, invisible .unavailable-note geometry-only compact scrollWidth, favicon.ico 404 -- not automatically in scope unless WU038 independently proves one is required). C008/C009/C010 remain pre-existing acknowledged historical packet-reference debt: reported separately, never repaired/suppressed/mutated/re-acknowledged, and alone never make AR-04 fail; any NEW graph integrity finding is blocking. No successor beyond WU040 is authorized; AR-05 and D7 remain not started.

ODM-014 - REPRODUCED. Mechanism: apps/research-explorer/src/records/recordIndex.ts:31-34 recordSearchText() builds the searchable string from only record.id, record.type, record.label and flattened summaryFields; its own comment states 'nothing else (no record-detail content; search never triggers a detail load)'. filterRecords() (recordIndex.ts:52-58) is the only search path and is consumed by RecordsTable.tsx:83-86. Compounding factor: the generated index label is truncated - 193 of 274 records (70%) have an ellipsis-terminated label, so even the label is only partially searchable. Measured coverage: searchable index text 73,104 chars vs canonical detail text 571,048 chars = ~12.8% of canonical content is reachable by search. Concrete canonical examples, verified by replaying the exact production normalize+match functions over generated/: 'conectividade rural-urbana' -> 0 search hits, present in EVD-000001 canonical detail; 'igualdade no acesso aos servicos' -> 0 hits, present in EVD-000001; 'deslocacao dentro do municipio' -> 0 hits, present in EVD-000001; 'prevalencia' -> 0 hits, present in 29 records; 'horarios' -> 2 hits but present in 12 records; 'MOB' -> 14 hits but present in 98 records. Whole canonical fields are unreachable, e.g. PRB problem_statement and causal_reading, and EVD observation.summary and inference_limits. Rendered browser confirmation: /?view=records&q=conectividade%20rural-urbana renders EmptyState 'Nenhum resultado.' with 0 rows while EVD-000001 contains that exact phrase.

ODM-015 - REPRODUCED. Mechanism is component remount / state ownership, NOT browser history. Sorting and pagination live in a component-local useReducer (RecordsTable.tsx:74, initialRecordsControllerState from recordsController.ts:23-26) and are deliberately excluded from URL state (recordsController.ts:5-12 comment; urlState.ts ExplorerUrlState carries only view, selectedId, query, typeFilter, graphDepth). RecordsExplorer.tsx:77-90 returns RecordDetailPanel INSTEAD OF RecordsTable when selectedId !== null, so selecting a record unmounts RecordsTable and destroys its reducer state; returning remounts it at initial state. Rendered browser reproduction at 1440x900: on /?view=records set sort=Tipo (aria-pressed=true, label 'Tipo up-arrow') and paged to 'Pagina 3 de 11'; clicked the first row -> URL ?view=records&id=EVD-000056; pressed browser Back -> URL correctly restored to ?view=records (history behaved correctly), but sort reverted to none (all four sort buttons aria-pressed=false) and pagination reverted to 'Pagina 1 de 11', first row back to EVD-000001. Both sort and pagination are lost; the loss is attributable to remount, not to history.

ODM-016 - REPRODUCED, two concrete and separate failures. Failure A - deep-link fragment never applied: navigating directly to /?view=records&id=EVD-000001#evd-sources at 360x740 left scrollY=128 while the #evd-sources target was still 1800px below the viewport top. Record detail is lazily loaded, so the fragment target does not exist in the DOM at the moment the browser performs its native fragment scroll, and nothing re-applies the fragment after content arrives. The same fragment applied correctly (scrollY=1761) when set after load, isolating the cause to load-order, not to a bad target. Failure B - sticky-header occlusion of fragment targets: at 360px .explorer-chrome is position:sticky with measured height 104px (index.css:2113-2125), but scroll-margin-top:108px is scoped to only two selectors, #overview-problemas and .problem-section, inside @media (max-width:767px) (index.css:2262-2267). Every other real fragment target has computed scroll-margin-top:0px. Measured at 360x740 with room to scroll: #evd-scope, #evd-limits and #evd-investigation each landed with their heading at top=0 versus headerBottom=104, i.e. 104px of the section heading hidden behind the sticky header. #evd-sources and #evd-technical were not occluded only because the document hit its scroll limit. These targets are reached by real in-app UI: SectionIndexList (presentation/SectionIndexList.tsx:19) renders ordinary anchor links to them, and RecordDetailPanel.tsx:826 links to #relacoes. Failure B was additionally captured as rendered screenshot evidence at 360px showing mid-paragraph text cut off at the header edge with the section heading invisible. Focus note: fragment navigation left document.activeElement as BODY, so keyboard focus does not follow the fragment; this is recorded as observed context, and the contract deliberately does not redesign navigation.

ODM-017 - REPRODUCED, measured objectively, not visually guessed. Method: WCAG 2.1 relative-luminance contrast computed in-browser from live getComputedStyle color and the nearest non-transparent ancestor background, over elements owning direct text nodes, with the correct large-text threshold applied (3.0 only for >=24px, or >=18.66px bold; otherwise 4.5). Every failure resolves to exactly one production token, --ink-faintest = #8a8578 = rgb(138,133,120) (index.css:653). Independent static computation of the production palette agrees: --ink-faintest scores 3.47:1 on --canvas, 3.68:1 on --surface, 3.31:1 on --surface-muted, 3.20:1 on --surface-chip; all below the 4.5:1 required for the sizes actually used (11px, 12px, 14.08px - none qualify as large text). Rendered failures by surface: Overview and Records - nav button 'Grafo' 3.47:1 at 14.08px; Problem - .problem-identity-id 3.47, header fact DT 3.47, file-path CODE 3.47, .effect-summary-counts 3.31, .effect-count 3.31, .open-question-evidence-refs-label 3.47; History - .problem-identity-id 3.47; EVD detail - .evd-secondary-id 3.47, lineage CODE 3.29, DT 3.47, scope SMALL 3.47, PRB CODE 3.29; SRC detail - identifier CODE 3.68. Two further declared low-contrast tokens, --ink-disclaimer (2.43:1) and --icon-muted (2.00:1), are declared in index.css but have zero usages, so they are not part of the reproduced defect. This is a functional accessibility correction confined to one token value, explicitly not a visual redesign.

ODM-019 - REPRODUCED. Mechanism: apps/research-explorer/src/records/EvdDetail.tsx:120 renders the button labelled 'Ver Problema ->' with onClick={() => onSelect(use.detail.id)}. onSelect is threaded from Explorer.tsx:94 as url.setSelectedId, which changes only selectedId and leaves view=records, so the user lands on the generic technical Detail for the PRB. The correct existing navigation path already exists and is used by every other 'go to the Problem experience' affordance: onViewAsProblem -> url.setViewAndSelection('problem', id) (Explorer.tsx:99, 124, 138), which is exactly what ContextTabs' 'Problema' tab (navigation/ContextTabs.tsx:22) and GraphExplorer's 'Ver como Problema' (GraphExplorer.tsx:343) already call. Rendered browser reproduction: from /?view=records&id=EVD-000001, clicking '.evd-problem-action' produced URL ?view=records&id=PRB-0001, document heading 'Detalhes', .problem-view absent, and ContextTabs reporting Detalhe=page (Problema and Historico not current) - i.e. technical Detail, not the Problem experience.

ODM-020 - REPRODUCED as a presentation ambiguity. What is currently shown: App.tsx:64-67 renders a single global line 'Corpus: {N} registos - gerado em <time dateTime={manifest.generatedAt}>'. Rendered browser value: 'Corpus: 274 registos - gerado em 10/09/2026, 18:59' with dateTime 2026-09-10T17:59:52.370Z. Why it can be mistaken for research freshness: manifest.generatedAt is assigned generatedAt: now() at data-build time in apps/research-explorer/scripts/build-data.js:123, so it is pure build wall-clock and advances on every rebuild even when no canonical research changed - it was 18:59 in this session purely because build-data was re-run. It carries no qualifier distinguishing build/generation time from research currency, and it sits immediately adjacent to corpus counts and to the Overview line 'investigacao em atualizacao continua' (Overview.tsx:165), so a reader can reasonably read the timestamp as 'the research was updated at this time'. Per-record canonical dates are separate and already correctly labelled where shown (e.g. EVD 'Extraida pela Open Evora em ...', EvdDetail.tsx:131). The required correction is presentation-only labelling/qualification; canonical research semantics and timestamps must not change.

ODM-021 - REPRODUCED, and the existing architecture already supports the bounded fix. Mechanism: Overview.tsx:66-74 renders ErrorNotice with title and message but passes NO action prop, while the sibling RecordsExplorer.tsx:62-75 passes action={<button onClick={indexState.retry}>Tentar novamente</button>} for the identical error shape. Both consume the same hook, and useRecordIndex already returns a retry function (records/useRecordIndex.ts:21,43) that bumps an attempt counter re-running the effect - Overview.tsx:33 already calls useRecordIndex and simply discards retry. ErrorNotice already accepts a caller-owned action node (presentation/ErrorNotice.tsx:34,50). Rendered browser reproduction with index.json aborted: Overview shows role=alert 'Falha ao carregar a visao geral' with buttonsInside=[] and no retry-like control anywhere on the page; the same interception on Records shows 'Tentar novamente', and clicking it after restoring the route fully recovered the view (alert gone, 25 rows rendered), proving the retry path is bounded, already implemented, and effective.

WU033 IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT - ODM-016 (deep-link/fragment/header). Files: apps/research-explorer/src/index.css (scroll-margin-top scope) and the record/problem detail mount path (src/records/RecordDetailPanel.tsx and/or src/app/Explorer.tsx) for post-load fragment application. WU033 IMPLEMENTATION CONTRACT - ODM-017 (contrast). Files: apps/research-explorer/src/index.css, token --ink-faintest (line 653) only. Prefer correcting the single token value over per-selector overrides so all fifteen usages are fixed once. This is a minimal accessibility correction, explicitly not a redesign: do not change typography, spacing, layout, hierarchy, or any other token. Regression test: a deterministic contrast assertion over the corrected token pair values (pure computation, no browser needed) so the ratio cannot silently regress. Rendered verification and accessibility verification: re-run the same measured in-browser contrast sweep over Overview, Records, Problem, History, EVD detail and SRC detail at desktop and 360px and assert zero remaining sub-threshold text.

ACCESSIBILITY VERIFICATION MECHANISM DECISION (no tooling added, none required for WU033). Smallest sufficient existing mechanisms, in order of preference: (1) Rendered browser verification via the already-available Playwright MCP browser, computing WCAG 2.1 contrast in-page from getComputedStyle - this is what produced the ODM-017 measurements here, requires no dependency, and objectively measures rather than guesses; (2) a deterministic pure-computation contrast assertion in the existing Vitest suite over the token pair values, which pins the corrected --ink-faintest against regression with no browser; (3) the existing @storybook/addon-a11y (already a devDependency, already enabled in .storybook/main.ts) for component-level axe checks and for keyboard/focus exercise. IMPORTANT LIMITATION for owner awareness: .storybook/preview.ts imports src/styles/tokens.css, which is a Storybook-only candidate palette explicitly documented as NOT imported by the production app; it does not import the production src/index.css where --ink-faintest lives. Storybook's a11y addon therefore cannot currently observe the production contrast defect, so it must not be treated as the primary ODM-017 gate. Mechanisms (1) and (2) together are sufficient and are the named contract mechanism. NO new persistent accessibility tooling (no axe-core, no jest-axe, no Lighthouse, no contrast linter) is required for WU033 and none is recommended at this time.
